factsAccepted: Junior turnover doubled (10% → 18% in two years). Exit interviews suggest junior consultants leaving for Big Four strategy roles or corporate positions. Partnership track is narrow: only 2 out of 10 hired consultants reach partner level. This creates perception of limited career advancement.

Revenue growth slowing (8% YoY, down from higher historical growth), EBITDA margin compressing toward 12% from historical 15%+. Partner utilization at 72% (below peer 75-80%), suggesting bench time or suboptimal project staffing. Realization rate 85% (below target 90%), indicating discount pressure or project profitability issues.

Boutique firm facing consolidation pressure; Big Four expanding in strategy. Client concentration risk: top 3 = 32% of revenue. Limited differentiation vs. larger competitors; pricing pressure from Big Four. Market perception: boutique = smaller, less resourced, riskier than Big Four.
factsNeedingClarification: Junior consultant feedback: Why are they leaving? Compensation? Career path? Fit/culture?
Partner productivity variance: Do some partners generate higher revenue than others? What differentiates?
Client profitability: Which clients are most profitable? Are low-margin clients driving utilization down?
Market positioning: How is firm differentiated from Big Four? Why should juniors stay for partnership track?
